prompts.name: map_from_image
prompts.title: Draw a map from a picture
prompts.description: Recreate a reference picture (screenshot, render or hand sketch) as a tile map with the user's tilesets and stamps.

arguments.name: reference
arguments.description: Absolute path of the picture (.png/.jpg/.webp), or a referenceId from get_session.references.

arguments.name: map
arguments.description: Map name or id to draw on (default: the active map).

prompts.template:
Recreate the picture {{reference}} as a tile map on {{map}} in Harita. Use only Harita tools (no shell, Python or files). Do not trace the picture by eye: the quantizer is cell-exact.

1. get_session: map id, layers, smart sources (smart) and references. If {{reference}} is a file path, call reference_add {path}; if it is already in references, use its referenceId.
2. reference_view {referenceId, mapId} to read the picture on the map grid. Look at the art: get_tile_catalog for each tileset, list_stamps {includeSheet:true}.
3. begin_edit {mapIds:[mapId], requestLabel}. Keep transactionId and resumeToken.
4. reference_quantize {referenceId, mapId}. For a flat-colour sketch use mode:"sketch" with colorLegend: each colour → {random:[main tile weight 8, 1–2 similar weight 1–2]} for grass, a tile, a tag word or {stampId} (houses, trees, bridge; match roof colours to the stamp sheet). Paint it with paint_grid {proposalId} (do not retype the rows).
5. Render or screenshot (high confidence): keep the quantized cells. Sketch: place_stamp every entry of its stamps list, redraw rivers and roads with draw_path (smart source from get_session.smart, points at the bends; river width 3, road 2) and ponds with smart_brush mode area, then place_stamp where the sketch has houses, trees and bridges.
6. render_compare {referenceId, mapId, mode:"side"}; fix the listed mismatches with paint_grid / replace_tiles / clear_region; zoom into bridge ends and joins; repeat until it matches.
7. validate_map (read hints), finish_edit {summary}, and tell the user the draft waits for Onayla.

prompts.name: map_from_text
prompts.title: Draw a map from a description
prompts.description: Design a tile map from a text description with the user's tilesets and stamps.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: What to draw, e.g. 'a village with a river, a bridge, a road and five houses'.

arguments.name: map
arguments.description: Map name or id to draw on (default: the active map).

prompts.template:
Draw this on {{map}} in Harita: {{description}}
Use only Harita tools (no shell, Python or files). Aim for a hand-made level, not a diagram.

1. get_session: map id, layers, smart sources (smart). get_tile_catalog for each tileset and list_stamps {includeSheet:true} to see the art and stamp sizes.
2. Plan in map cells (x right, y down): water and main roads first, then a cluster of buildings along the road, fields/gardens, tree clumps and edge forest. Keep paths connected and leave 1–2 cells around stamps.
3. begin_edit {mapIds:[mapId], requestLabel}. Keep transactionId and resumeToken.
4. Ground: one paint_rect over the whole map with value {random:[main grass weight 8, 1–2 similar variants weight 1–2]}.
5. Water and roads: draw_path with a smart source (points at the bends; width 3 for a river, 2 for a main road), ponds with smart_brush mode area. Draw a road that crosses water straight across in one draw_path, then place the bridge stamp over the crossing, covering the full water width.
6. Buildings, trees and fences: place_stamp (positions for many copies). Give every door a 1-wide draw_path to the road; fences as closed outlines around a field or garden; trees in clumps.
7. Details on the upper layer: bushes, flowers, rocks with paint_cells points near paths and houses, so no large area stays empty.
8. render_preview {grid:true, coordinates:true}; zoom into joins; fix with paint_grid / replace_tiles / clear_region.
9. validate_map (read hints), finish_edit {summary}, and tell the user the draft waits for Onayla.
